types.explanation: RFC 3207 specifies that a 220 reply to STARTTLS indicates the server is ready for TLS negotiation.
RFC 3030 BDAT and RFC 1985 ETRN examples use 250 to indicate successful command processing.

types.type_name: Unable to process ETRN command at this time
types.explanation: RFC 1985 identifies the 458 response as the ETRN error response when queue processing cannot be started.
RFC 3207 requires 530 in response to commands other than NOOP, EHLO, STARTTLS, or QUIT before TLS is established.
RFC 3463 defines 5.7.0 as other or undefined security status; RFC 3207 specifies it as the enhanced status for the 530 STARTTLS-required reply.
RFC 3463 defines X.2.0 as other or undefined mailbox status.
RFC 3463 defines X.2.1 as mailbox disabled, not accepting messages.
RFC 3463 defines X.2.2 as mailbox full.
RFC 3463 defines X.3.5 as system incorrectly configured.
